scope: Where ports and adapters benefit a complete planned capability refactor; research only
position: Extend the existing hexagonal design at meaningful business/technical boundaries. A complete coordinated refactor is feasible as one delivery, while dependency-ordered implementation and checks remain necessary inside that delivery.
already_present: HTTP controllers consume service contracts and implement generated HTTP interface; HTTP/socket/CLI are different driving adapters.
Repository ports separate application calls from SQLite/sqlc; generated records and database/sql stay in adapters.
Context propagation, explicit logger/repository injection, command composition and generic bootstrap lifecycle already establish important boundaries.

concrete_gaps.area: Shared use case behind JSON and native
concrete_gaps.evidence: transcripts.go:94–155 converts modern input into opcode500 and reads packet acknowledgment
concrete_gaps.target: A typed chat command/result shared by native decoder and JSON controller; protocol serialization belongs to native compatibility adapter.

concrete_gaps.evidence: page_routes.go and domain.PageRequest/PageResult mix method/URL/form and HTML/status into application contracts
concrete_gaps.target: Compatibility adapter validates original selectors/forms and renders templ from typed use-case results; both direct HTTP and opcode922/923 call this adapter. Preserve authentication/error ordering and literal routes.
Each capability owns only repository and collaborator contracts required by its use cases. The same SQLite Store may implement several; no database split is necessary.

concrete_gaps.evidence: Account/session objects mix credential cache and delivery gates; packets occupy push/inflight structures
concrete_gaps.target: An explicit realtime/session owner exposes typed session/admission/delivery operations; identity and contacts do not receive mutable maps or copied mutexes. Retain one ordering owner while protocol envelopes move outward.

concrete_gaps.evidence: SaveMessage and CreditOperationWithNote combine pure validation with transaction-sensitive checks
concrete_gaps.target: Extract reusable pure business policies into owning capabilities. Keep authoritative membership, balance, block and ownership decisions within the atomic persistence operation or explicit transaction-bound workflow to prevent TOCTOU bugs.

concrete_gaps.evidence: nativeProviderMessage records local/mock requests; OTP is development-only
concrete_gaps.target: Use outbound ports for actual delivery/verification/payment capabilities when their use cases need them, with honest recorded/no-send mock adapters. Do not rename mock request persistence as a successful external delivery.

concrete_gaps.evidence: domain includes PageRequest/Result and API-shaped results, not only business concepts
concrete_gaps.target: Place representation DTOs at adapters and business command/result/value types with their capability; retain a small explicit shared vocabulary where needed.

proposed_dependency_direction: Generated HTTP routing -> controllers -> typed capability application ports/use cases
Native socket or HTTP tunnel -> native compatibility adapter -> same typed use cases
Historical HTTP pages or opcode922 -> legacy page adapter -> typed use cases -> legacy templ renderer
SQLite/sqlc and mock/provider implementations -> implement those outbound contracts
cmd/internal/wiring -> concrete composition; bootstrap -> supplied lifecycle hooks only

reasonable_ports.note: Authentication/authorization remains enforced in application policy; a raw caller-supplied username is not trusted authority.
Keep message/audience/key and current durable authorization checks atomic.
Contract includes initial roster; no independent account and contact commits.
Contract includes ledger, entitlement, gift note and durable message intent.

reasonable_ports.example: ResolveSession / validate room participation / reserve-and-complete delivery as actual workflows require
reasonable_ports.note: Do not expose mutable session maps, Packet channels, or naked locks to business modules; coordinate block/write ordering.

reasonable_ports.example: Verification delivery or payment authorization only for currently supported use cases
reasonable_ports.note: Mocks retain truthful pending/local behavior and do not imply providers are implemented.

avoid_abstraction: A port interface for every helper, formatter, value object or static catalog lookup.
A custom logger interface when *slog.Logger already provides the needed concrete dependency.
A generic CRUD repository or UnitOfWork covering all features without a concrete workflow need.
Putting *sql.Tx or generated sqlc rows in domain/application ports.
Introducing an asynchronous event bus to replace synchronous atomic operations.
Separate session stores or locks per new capability merely to make package folders independent.
Treating every inbound port as requiring a Go interface; exported concrete methods are also valid application boundaries and interfaces should follow consumers.
one_delivery_plan_constraints: Define target contracts, ownership and completion criteria before parallel file movement.
Move shared commands/results and pure policy first; wire complete capabilities behind stable adapters in dependency order.
Keep atomic persistence contracts and current lock ordering through the move; changing concurrency policy is not required for new package ownership.
Preserve existing endpoints, packet semantics, native error ordering, keyed-message canonical serialization and old database contents.
Run focused checks as boundaries move and full race/vet/native acceptance against one final graph.

Remove temporary facades or explicitly reduce them to representation/dispatch ownership by the delivery end; do not leave the old Application containing all business methods and call the folder move complete.

sources.supports: Application behavior can be driven through several adapters and tested independently of UI/database; the conceptual inside/outside boundary matters more than a prescribed folder layout.
Interfaces generally belong with consumers; return concrete implementations and add contracts for demonstrated needs rather than speculative interfaces.
Package purpose and exported APIs guide boundaries; directory hierarchy alone creates no semantic relationship.
Generated queries can bind to the same transaction; package refactoring does not require independent commits or leaking SQL types into application code.

local_evidence.finding: HTTP controllers depend on application service ports; generated ServerInterface is implemented here.
NativeService exposes protocol.Packet, packet queues and transport write gates.
Typed chat input/output port already exists, but it is implemented through native packets internally.
SendChatMessage constructs opcode500, calls native messageWithFormatting, and interprets packet acknowledgment/error.
Account embeds deliveryGate; session and Application own shared authentication/presence/room/queue state.
messageWithFormatting mixes protocol decoding, validation, permissions, photo handling, slash commands, persistence and live delivery.
Page handlers take method/URL/form and return rendered pages inside services.
PageRequest/PageResult encode HTTP-like request and document representation concerns in shared domain package.
Provider messages currently validate and record mock requests; no actual external send.
Atomic message save includes membership/blocks and other durable invariant checks, audience and idempotency.
Gift operation preserves ledger/inventory/note/message intent in one transaction.
Registration creates account and initial roster atomically.
Worker Run owns timed session/vote maintenance and joins it on shutdown.
Existing guards exclude infrastructure imports from application but explicitly permit protocol in services; remaining compatibility coupling is intentional current scope.
